_comment: HTTP hardening contract -- ADR-0068. Features 30 (response model) and 44 (file upload).
Two defects from a security audit of the Python reference, with relatives in the
other three frameworks:
HDR-CRLF: Response header(), cookie() and redirect() accepted CR, LF and NUL, and
the built-in server wrote header lines to the socket as it found them. Cookie
names and values were not validated at all. Now a header name that is not an
HTTP token, or a header value / redirect location / cookie name, value or
attribute carrying CR, LF or NUL (and ';' for cookies), is REFUSED at the call
site with the exact ADR-0068 message -- never stripped. The built-in server
checks again before writing (500 'Invalid response header').
BODY-CAP: the built-in server read the whole declared body before
TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE was checked. Now the head is capped by
TINA4_MAX_REQUEST_HEADER (431), a declared length over the cap is refused
before a body byte is read (413), the body is read in bounded chunks under a
running count (chunked included), invalid framing answers 400, a stalled
partial request answers 408, and every rejection has one JSON + security
header shape.
Every case runs against the real framework with no mocks: the response cases
against the real response object, the server cases against a real server
booted as a child process over a real loopback socket, with RSS read from the
operating system.
Shared suite names: Python tests/test_http_hardening_contract.py, PHP
tests/HttpHardeningContractTest.php, Ruby spec/http_hardening_contract_spec.rb,
Node test/httpHardeningContract.test.ts. A framework adds itself to 'suites' in
the change that makes its suite carry every case of that invariant.
feature: 30 / 44 - Response headers refuse CR, LF and NUL; built-in servers enforce the upload cap before reading the body

messages.header_name: Header name must be a valid HTTP token ["<name>"]
messages.cookie_name: Cookie name must be a valid HTTP token ["<name>"]
messages.name_placeholder: <name> is the caller's name written as a JSON string literal

transport_rejections.cause: bare CR, LF or NUL in the head
declared or running body past TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE

transport_rejections.body: {"error":"Request timed out before it was complete"}

transport_rejections.cause: unsafe response header reached the writer

invariants.rule: A response header whose name is not an HTTP token, or whose value contains CR, LF or NUL, is refused at the call site with the exact ADR-0068 message naming the header. The same holds for a redirect location (named Location), an explicit content type and a download filename. Nothing is stripped or encoded silently. Ordinary values still set normally.
invariants.why: header() and redirect() accepted CR/LF and the built-in server wrote them raw, so user input reaching a header could end it early and start another. Node's setHeader already throws ERR_INVALID_CHAR; the other three now match it. Mutation: remove the call-site check and the refusal cases go red.
cases: a header value containing cr lf or nul is refused
a header name that is not a token is refused
a redirect location containing cr or lf is refused
normal headers and redirects still work

invariants.rule: A cookie whose name is not an HTTP token, or whose value or any attribute value contains CR, LF, NUL or ';', is refused at the call site with the exact ADR-0068 cookie message. Ordinary cookies still set, and several Set-Cookie headers on one response all reach the client. A framework that already percent-encodes the cookie value (Ruby, Node) keeps encoding it instead of refusing; attribute values are refused in all four.
invariants.why: Cookie names and values were not validated, so a ';' in a value added attributes the application never set, and CR/LF started a new header. Mutation: remove the cookie check and the refusal case goes red.
cases: a cookie name value or attribute that could inject is refused
multiple set cookie headers all reach the client

invariants.rule: A header that reaches the built-in server's socket writer by another path (appended to the header list directly) and carries CR, LF or NUL, or a non-token name, is never written. The server answers 500 with the transport rejection shape and body {"error":"Invalid response header"} and logs the header name.
invariants.why: Defence in depth: framework internals and direct appends bypass the call-site check. Mutation: remove the writer check and the injected header appears on the wire.
cases: the built in server refuses to write an unsafe header

invariants.rule: The built-in server answers 413 to a declared Content-Length over TINA4_MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE before reading a body byte, reads every body in bounded chunks under a running count (chunked included) and answers 413 the moment the count passes the cap, so the server's memory does not grow with what a client declares or sends. A body under the cap is still served.
invariants.why: The asyncio fallback server read the whole declared body before the cap was checked; a large declared body sent slowly grew RSS without a ceiling. Chunked bodies were ignored. Mutation: go back to one read of the declared length and the memory case goes red.
cases: a declared content length over the cap is refused before the body is read
an oversized declared body does not grow server memory
a chunked body over the cap is refused as it arrives
a chunked body under the cap is decoded and served
a body under the cap is still served

invariants.rule: The built-in server answers 400 to a Content-Length that is not ASCII digits or two that disagree, to Transfer-Encoding other than exactly chunked or combined with Content-Length, and to a head carrying a bare CR, LF or NUL; 431 to a head past TINA4_MAX_REQUEST_HEADER; 408 to a partial request silent for TINA4_REQUEST_TIMEOUT. Each closes cleanly and the server keeps serving.
invariants.why: A non-numeric Content-Length raised an uncaught ValueError and an oversized head an uncaught LimitOverrunError, each leaking the socket; a stalled body raised an uncaught timeout. Mutation: drop the Content-Length validation and the 400 case goes red.
cases: conflicting content length and transfer encoding answer 400
a request head with a bare line feed answers 400
the server keeps serving after every rejection

invariants.rule: Every built-in server transport rejection (400, 408, 413, 431, 500) carries the exact ADR-0068 status and JSON body, Content-Type application/json, Content-Length, Connection: close and the canonical security header set without Strict-Transport-Security. The ASGI path's 413 in Python carries the same bytes.
invariants.why: One shape for every early refusal, so a client, a proxy and a test can read them the same way in all four frameworks, and a refusal is still a response that carries the security headers.
cases: a transport rejection carries the json body and security headers

invariants.rule: PHP, Ruby and Node carry every case above in their own suite, and each adds itself to the invariants' suites as it lands.
invariants.why: Owed ledger entry: the contract is written in Python first. PHP is in progress on fix/refuse-header-crlf; Ruby and Node are owed.
